summary: A light, rhythmic march on the spot that raises your heart rate and warms up the legs before training.
steps: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and your arms relaxed at your sides.
Lift one knee to a comfortable height while the opposite arm swings forward.
Lower that foot softly and lift the other knee, swinging the other arm.
Keep alternating at an easy, steady rhythm with a light bounce through the feet.
mistakes: Stomping heavily instead of landing softly
Slouching or leaning back as you lift the knees

summary: A standing mobility drill that rolls the hips in slow, wide circles to loosen the hips and lower back.
steps: Stand with feet a little wider than hip width, knees soft, hands on your hips.
Push your hips forward, then sweep them out to one side.
Carry them back behind you, sticking your bottom out, then round to the other side.
Keep the circle slow and wide, with your shoulders staying roughly over your feet.
After a few circles, reverse the direction.
mistakes: Bending sideways at the waist instead of moving the hips

summary: A rocking drill that drives the knee forward over the foot to improve ankle dorsiflexion and loosen the calves.
steps: Kneel in a half-kneeling position with your front foot flat on the floor.
Shift your weight forward, moving the front knee over the middle of the foot.
Keep the heel down and pause for a moment at the end of your comfortable range.
Rock back to the start and continue, then switch sides.
mistakes: Letting the heel lift off the floor

summary: A gentle hands-on-floor hold that prepares the wrists and forearms to bear weight for push and handstand work.
steps: Kneel on all fours with your hands under your shoulders and fingers spread wide.
Press the whole palm and the base of each finger into the floor.
Slowly shift your weight forward over your hands until you feel a mild load in the wrists.
Hold the position, breathing steadily.
mistakes: Lifting the base of the fingers off the floor
Dropping weight onto the wrists too quickly

summary: A straight-arm push-up variation that moves only the shoulder blades, training scapular control for pushing.
steps: Set up in a high plank with your hands under your shoulders and your arms locked.
Let your chest sink slightly so the shoulder blades draw together.
Push the floor away to spread the shoulder blades apart and round the upper back slightly.
Return to the start with control, keeping the elbows straight throughout.
mistakes: Bending the elbows into a partial push-up
Dropping the head between the arms

summary: A fundamental two-leg squat that builds strength in the quadriceps and glutes and grooves a sound squat pattern.
steps: Stand with your feet about hip- to shoulder-width apart, toes turned out slightly.
Bend your hips and knees together to sit down between your heels.
Lower as deep as you can while keeping your chest up and heels on the floor.
Push through your whole foot to stand tall at the top.
mistakes: Chest collapsing forward at the bottom

summary: A rear-foot-elevated split squat that loads the front leg to build single-leg quadriceps and glute strength.
steps: Stand a long stride in front of a bench and rest the top of your rear foot on it.
Keep your torso tall and your weight mostly on the front foot.
Bend the front knee to lower until the back knee nearly touches the floor.
Drive through the front foot to return to the top.
Switch sides.
mistakes: Pushing off with the rear leg
Front heel lifting off the floor

summary: A full-depth single-leg squat with the free leg held straight in front, building leg strength, balance and control.
steps: Stand on one leg with the other leg extended slightly in front of you.
Reach your arms forward and bend the standing knee to sit down slowly.
Lift the free leg higher as you descend so it stays clear of the floor.
Lower to full depth without collapsing, keeping the heel down.
Drive through the standing foot to rise to the top, then switch sides.
mistakes: Dropping into the bottom without control
Standing heel lifting off the floor

summary: A single-leg squat with the free foot held behind you, building quadriceps and glute strength with a tall torso.
steps: Stand on one leg and bend the other knee to hold that foot behind you.
Reach the free arm forward for balance.
Bend the standing knee to lower until the back knee lightly touches the floor.
Drive through the standing foot to return to the top.
Switch sides.
mistakes: Dropping the back knee hard onto the floor
Leaning far forward to reach depth

summary: A deep side-to-side squat that strengthens the quadriceps and adductors while building hip mobility.
steps: Stand with your feet in a wide stance, toes turned out slightly.
Shift your weight to one side and sit down into that hip, bending the knee.
Keep the other leg straight with its toes pointing up as you lower.
Push through the bent leg to return to the middle.
Repeat to the other side.
cues: Heel down on the working side
mistakes: Working heel lifting off the floor
Rounding the back to reach depth

summary: A single-leg step onto a raised surface that builds quadriceps and glute strength and balance.
steps: Stand facing a sturdy box or step and place one whole foot on top.
Lean slightly forward and drive through the top foot to stand up on the step.
Stand tall at the top without pushing off the bottom foot.
Lower the trailing foot back to the floor with control.
Switch sides.
mistakes: Pushing off with the bottom leg
Knee caving inward as you rise
Dropping down quickly instead of lowering

summary: A backward-stepping lunge that strengthens the quadriceps and glutes of the front leg with steady balance.
steps: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart.
Step one foot back and lower until both knees bend to about 90 degrees.
Keep your torso upright and the front knee in line with the toes.
Push through the front foot to bring the back foot forward and stand.
Alternate legs or switch sides.
mistakes: Back knee slamming into the floor

summary: A pattern drill that teaches bending at the hips with a neutral spine, training the hamstrings and glutes.
steps: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and a soft bend in the knees.
Push your hips back as your torso tips forward, keeping your spine long.
Lower until you feel tension in the hamstrings or your back begins to round.
Drive the hips forward to stand tall, squeezing the glutes.
mistakes: Bending the knees into a squat
Overarching the back at the top

summary: A kneeling hamstring exercise where you lower your body slowly forward, building eccentric hamstring strength.
steps: Kneel on a pad with your ankles anchored under a sturdy object or held by a partner.
Keep a straight line from knees to head and squeeze your glutes.
Lean forward slowly, resisting with your hamstrings for as long as possible.
Catch yourself with your hands in a push-up position when you can no longer hold.
Push lightly off the floor to return to kneeling.
mistakes: Bending at the hips instead of staying straight
Dropping quickly instead of resisting the descent

summary: A two-leg heel raise that strengthens the calves and builds control around the ankle.
steps: Stand on the floor or the edge of a step with the balls of your feet supported.
Rise onto your toes by lifting your heels as high as you can.
Pause briefly at the top.
Lower your heels slowly through the full range without dropping.
mistakes: Rolling onto the outer edges of the feet

summary: A one-leg heel raise that strengthens each calf on its own and improves ankle stability.
steps: Stand on one foot on the floor or a step, touching a wall lightly for balance.
Rise onto the ball of the foot as high as you can.
Pause briefly at the top.
Lower the heel slowly through the full range.
Switch sides.

summary: A handstand held with the chest facing a wall, building shoulder strength, body alignment and comfort upside down.
steps: Place your hands on the floor shoulder-width apart, close to a wall, facing it.
Walk your feet up the wall as you walk your hands closer to it.
Stack your hands, shoulders and hips with your body straight and toes on the wall.
Push the floor away and keep the ribs tucked.
Hold the position, breathing steadily, then walk down with control.
mistakes: Arching the lower back into a banana shape
Hands placed too far from the wall

summary: A pike push-up with the feet raised that loads the shoulders and triceps in a near-vertical pressing angle.
steps: Place your feet on a box or bench and your hands on the floor, hips high in a pike.
Stack your hips above your shoulders as closely as you can.
Bend your elbows to lower the top of your head toward the floor in front of your hands.
Press back up until your arms are straight.
cues: Head lands ahead of the hands
mistakes: Hips dropping so it becomes a decline push-up
Elbows flaring straight out to the sides
Dropping the head quickly to the floor

summary: Practice kicking up to a handstand without support, building balance, shoulder strength and safe exits.
steps: Stand in a lunge with your arms overhead and plenty of clear space around you.
Place your hands on the floor and kick one leg up, bringing the other to meet it.
Find balance with a straight body, using finger pressure to stop overbalancing.
Hold the position, breathing steadily.
Exit by stepping down or cartwheeling out when balance is lost.
mistakes: Kicking too hard and falling over
Bending the arms when balance is lost

summary: A floor-based hip lift that strengthens the glutes while keeping the ribs down and the spine neutral.
steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent, feet flat and hip-width apart.
Brace lightly and press through your heels to lift your hips.
Rise until there is a straight line from knees to shoulders and squeeze your glutes.
Lower your hips slowly back to the floor.
mistakes: Arching the lower back at the top
Pushing through the toes instead of the heels

summary: A lying core drill that extends opposite arm and leg while the lower back stays down, training anti-extension.
steps: Lie on your back with your arms pointing up and knees bent to 90 degrees over your hips.
Press your lower back gently into the floor.
Slowly extend one arm overhead and the opposite leg out, stopping before the back lifts.
Return to the start and repeat with the other arm and leg.
mistakes: Lower back arching off the floor
Moving too fast to stay controlled

summary: A lying core hold with arms and legs lifted and the lower back pressed down, building trunk tension for skills.
steps: Lie on your back with your legs straight and arms by your sides.
Press your lower back into the floor and draw your ribs down.
Lift your shoulders and legs off the floor, reaching the arms overhead if you can.
Hold the position, breathing steadily.
cues: Arms by ears if you can
mistakes: Lower back lifting off the floor

summary: A hanging core exercise that lifts the knees toward the chest, training the abdominals and grip.
steps: Hang from a bar with straight arms and your shoulders active.
Brace your core and lift your knees toward your chest.
Curl the pelvis up slightly at the top without swinging.
Lower your legs slowly to a still hang.
mistakes: Leaning the torso back instead of curling up

summary: A straight-arm hang from a bar that builds grip strength and shoulder tolerance for pulling work.
steps: Grip a bar with an overhand grip about shoulder-width apart.
Lift your feet so you hang with straight arms.
Draw your shoulders slightly away from your ears and keep your legs still.
Hold the position, breathing steadily.

summary: A small pull from a dead hang using only the shoulder blades, building scapular strength for pull-ups.
steps: Hang from a bar with an overhand grip and straight arms.
Pull your shoulder blades down and back to lift your body slightly.
Pause briefly at the top with the arms still straight.
Lower slowly back to a full hang.
mistakes: Shrugging the shoulders up to the ears

summary: A strict vertical pull from a full hang to chin over the bar, building lat and biceps strength.
steps: Hang from a bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Set your shoulders down and brace your core with your legs still.
Pull your chest toward the bar until your chin clears it.
Lower slowly to a full hang with straight arms.
mistakes: Stopping short of a full hang
Reaching the chin forward to clear the bar

summary: A pull-up that transitions over the bar into a dip, building explosive pulling and pushing strength.
steps: Hang from a bar with an overhand grip about shoulder-width apart.
Pull explosively, driving the bar toward your lower chest and hips toward the bar.
As the bar reaches your chest, lean forward and turn your wrists over the bar.
Press down into a dip until your arms lock out above the bar.
Lower back through the transition to a hang with control.
mistakes: Pulling straight up instead of around the bar
Leading with one arm through the transition
Dropping from the top without control

summary: A push-up performed standing against a wall, introducing the pressing pattern for the chest, shoulders and triceps.
steps: Stand an arm's length from a wall and place your hands on it at shoulder height.
Step your feet back slightly so your body forms a straight line.
Bend your elbows to bring your chest toward the wall.
Push the wall away until your arms are straight.
mistakes: Dropping the head toward the wall

summary: The classic floor push-up from a high plank, building chest, shoulder and triceps strength with a rigid trunk.
steps: Set up in a high plank with hands slightly wider than shoulders and body straight.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes.
Bend your elbows to lower your chest until it nearly touches the floor.
Push through your palms to return to straight arms.
mistakes: Elbows flaring straight out to the sides
Cutting the range short at the bottom

summary: A push-up with the hands set well outside the shoulders, shifting more emphasis to the chest and front shoulders.
steps: Set up in a high plank with your hands placed wider than shoulder-width.
Brace your core so your body forms a straight line.
Lower your chest until it nearly touches the floor.
Drive through your palms to return to straight arms.
cues: Wrists under or just inside elbows
mistakes: Hands so wide the range becomes very short

summary: A close-hand push-up with thumbs and index fingers forming a diamond, placing heavy emphasis on the triceps.
steps: Set up in a plank with your hands under your chest, thumbs and index fingers touching.
Keep your body straight and your core tight.
Bend your elbows close to your sides to lower your chest toward your hands.
Push back up until your arms are fully straight.

summary: A push-up with the feet raised on a bench, shifting more load to the upper chest, shoulders and triceps.
steps: Place your feet on a bench or step and your hands on the floor slightly wider than shoulders.
Brace so your body forms a straight line from shoulders to ankles.
Bend your elbows to lower your chest toward the floor.
Push back up to straight arms.
mistakes: Hips sagging under the extra load
Piking the hips up to make it easier
Feet set too high for your strength

summary: A wide push-up that shifts the body toward one hand while the other arm stays straight, building one-arm strength.
steps: Set up in a high plank with your hands placed much wider than shoulder-width.
Bend one elbow to lower your chest toward that hand.
Keep the opposite arm straight, sliding or pivoting it out to the side.
Push back up to the middle and repeat toward the other side.

summary: A wide push-up that slides the chest from one hand to the other at the bottom, building strength in each arm.
steps: Set up in a high plank with your hands placed much wider than shoulder-width.
Lower your chest toward one hand, keeping the other arm straight.
Stay low and shift your chest across to the other hand.
Push back up to straight arms once you reach the far side.
mistakes: Rising up while moving side to side

summary: A push-up performed on a single arm with the feet set wide, building maximal chest, shoulder and triceps strength.
steps: Set up in a plank with your feet wider than shoulder-width and one hand under your chest.
Place your free hand behind your back.
Brace your whole body and lower your chest slowly toward the floor.
Press back up to a straight arm without rotating your torso.
Switch sides.
mistakes: Torso twisting open toward the free arm

summary: A push-up with the hands set near the hips and the shoulders leaned past the wrists, building strength for planche.
steps: Set up in a plank with your hands beside your waist, fingers turned out or back.
Lean forward until your shoulders are in front of your wrists.
Keep the lean as you bend your elbows to lower your chest.
Press back up, keeping the shoulders forward throughout.
mistakes: Losing the forward lean as you lower

summary: A flowing push-up that swoops from a downward-dog shape into an upward-facing arch, training pressing and mobility.
steps: Start in a pike with hips high, hands and feet slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Bend your elbows and swoop your chest down close to the floor between your hands.
Continue forward and straighten your arms to arch up, hips low and chest up.
Push your hips back up to return to the pike.
mistakes: Dropping the hips to the floor before the swoop
Rushing and losing control of the arch

summary: A push-up that moves between forearm plank and high plank, targeting the triceps like a bodyweight skull crusher.
steps: Set up in a forearm plank with elbows under your shoulders and body straight.
Press through your palms to lift the elbows and straighten your arms.
Lower your forearms back to the floor with control.
Keep your hips level and body straight throughout.
mistakes: Hips piking up to help the press
Elbows flaring out to the sides

summary: A straight-arm plank movement that protracts and retracts the shoulder blades to build scapular control.
steps: Set up in a high plank with hands under your shoulders and elbows locked.
Let your chest sink slightly so the shoulder blades move together.
Push the floor away to spread the shoulder blades apart.
Move through a comfortable, controlled range without bending the arms.

summary: A push-up that draws one knee toward the same-side elbow on each rep, adding core and hip work to the press.
steps: Set up in a high plank with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Lower your chest while bringing one knee out to the side toward the same elbow.
Push back up while returning the foot to the start.
Repeat with the other leg.
mistakes: Hips piking up as the knee moves

summary: A swooping push-up from pike to arch that reverses the same path back, training the chest, shoulders and triceps.
steps: Start in a pike with hips high and hands and feet slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Bend your elbows and swoop your chest down and forward close to the floor.
Straighten your arms into an arch with hips low and chest up.
Reverse the swoop, bending your elbows and sliding back to the pike.
mistakes: Pushing hips straight back instead of reversing the swoop

summary: A push-up on gymnastic rings where unstable handles demand extra chest, shoulder and stabilizer strength.
steps: Set the rings low and hold them in a high plank, arms straight and rings close to your sides.
Brace so your body forms a straight line.
Lower your chest between the rings, keeping them from drifting apart.
Press back up and turn the rings out slightly at the top.

summary: A push-up with hands set wide and low near the hips, an extreme straight-body press toward the maltese hold.
steps: Set up in a plank with your hands wide and near your hips, fingers pointing outward.
Lean your shoulders forward and protract your shoulder blades.
Bend your elbows to lower your chest toward the floor with the body straight.
Press back up while holding the lean.

summary: An explosive push-up that drives the hands off the floor for a clap, building upper-body power.
steps: Set up in a strong push-up position with hands slightly wider than shoulders.
Lower your chest under control.
Push explosively so your hands leave the floor and clap them quickly.
Land with soft elbows to absorb the impact, then reset.
mistakes: Not pushing high enough to clap

summary: An explosive push-up where both hands and feet leave the floor and the body extends in the air, building power.
steps: Set up in a high plank with your hands slightly wider than shoulders.
Lower your chest quickly with the body tight.
Push explosively through the hands and toes so both leave the floor.
Reach the arms forward briefly in the air, then return them under you.
Land with soft elbows and knees bent slightly.
mistakes: Arching the back in the air
Attempting it without a powerful clap push-up

summary: A push-up from an inverted V shape that lowers the head toward the floor, training the shoulders like a press.
steps: Start in a pike with hands shoulder-width apart and hips high over your shoulders.
Bend your elbows to lower the top of your head toward the floor ahead of your hands.
Keep the hips high as you lower.
Press back up until your arms are straight.
cues: Head forms a tripod with hands
mistakes: Hips dropping into a regular push-up
Lowering the head between the hands

summary: A vertical push-up in a wall-supported handstand, building strong shoulders and triceps for overhead pressing.
steps: Place your hands shoulder-width apart close to a wall and kick up into a handstand.
Keep your arms straight, body long and heels resting on the wall.
Bend your elbows to lower your head slowly toward the floor.
Press back up until your arms are straight.
cues: Head forms a tripod with hands

summary: A wall handstand push-up on raised handles so the head drops below the hands, adding range for the shoulders.
steps: Set parallettes or blocks close to a wall and kick up into a handstand on them.
Keep your body straight with heels on the wall.
Lower slowly until your head passes below the level of your hands.
Press back up to straight arms.
mistakes: Losing tension at the deepest point
Arching the back to press out
Using a deficit before the wall version is solid

summary: A handstand push-up performed without wall support, combining balance with heavy shoulder and triceps pressing.
steps: Kick up into a balanced freestanding handstand with hands shoulder-width apart.
Shift your shoulders slightly forward as you begin to bend the elbows.
Lower under control until your head nearly touches the floor.
Press back up, moving the shoulders back over the hands to regain balance.
mistakes: Losing balance and arching the back

summary: A handstand push-up lowered to a horizontal hold with the body parallel to the floor, then pressed back up.
steps: Start in a handstand on the floor or parallettes.
Lean the shoulders forward and bend the elbows as your body tilts down.
Lower until your body is parallel to the floor, elbows bent near 90 degrees.
Press back up and rotate the body to the vertical handstand.
mistakes: Bending at the hips instead of staying straight

summary: A dip with the hands on a bench behind you, training the triceps with the feet supporting part of your weight.
steps: Sit on the edge of a bench, hands beside your hips, fingers forward.
Slide your hips off the bench with your legs extended in front of you.
Bend your elbows straight back to lower your body to a comfortable depth.
Press through your hands to straighten your arms.
mistakes: Lowering past a comfortable shoulder range
Elbows flaring out to the sides

summary: A dip between parallel bars that lowers until the upper arms are about parallel, building triceps and chest strength.
steps: Support yourself on parallel bars with straight arms and shoulders pressed down.
Lower your body by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your sides.
Stop when your upper arms are about parallel to the floor.
Press back up until your arms are straight.

summary: A parallel bar dip with an intentional forward lean of the torso, shifting more emphasis to the chest.
steps: Support yourself on parallel bars with straight arms.
Lean your torso forward and let your legs drift slightly behind you.
Lower until your upper arms are about parallel, elbows angled slightly out.
Press back up while keeping the forward lean.
mistakes: Losing the lean and standing upright
Shoulders rolling forward at the bottom

summary: A dip on a single straight bar in front of the body, building the pressing strength used in muscle-ups.
steps: Support yourself above a straight bar with an overhand grip, arms locked.
Lean your chest forward over the bar and let your legs angle slightly forward.
Bend your elbows to lower your chest toward the bar.
Press back up to straight arms.
mistakes: Bar drifting away from the body

summary: A dip with a straight bar behind the body, demanding shoulder extension mobility and strong pressing.
steps: Stand with your back to a straight bar and grip it behind you with arms straight.
Support your weight with your hands and lift your feet so you hang in front of the bar.
Bend your elbows to lower your body, letting the bar travel up your back.
Press back up to straight arms.

summary: A dip on gymnastic rings that demands strong stabilization through the shoulders, chest and triceps.
steps: Support yourself on the rings with straight arms and rings close to your sides.
Turn the rings out slightly and keep your body still.
Lower until your upper arms are about parallel, keeping the rings close.
Press back up and lock out with the rings turned out.

summary: A parallel bar dip performed while holding the legs straight out in an L-sit, adding core and hip flexor work.
steps: Support yourself on parallel bars with straight arms.
Lift your straight legs in front of you to hip height.
Lower until your upper arms are about parallel while holding the legs up.
Press back up to straight arms without dropping the legs.

summary: A straight-arm plank hold with the shoulders leaned past the wrists, building shoulder and wrist strength for planche.
steps: Set up in a high plank with your fingers turned slightly out.
Protract your shoulder blades and tuck into a hollow body.
Lean forward until your shoulders are in front of your wrists, arms straight.
Hold the position, breathing steadily.

summary: A straight-arm balance with knees tucked and feet off the floor, an early planche progression for the shoulders.
steps: Squat down and place your hands on the floor or parallettes beside your feet.
Lean forward with straight arms until your feet become light.
Lift your feet and pull your knees into your chest, hips level with your shoulders.
Hold the position, breathing steadily.

summary: A planche held with the legs spread wide, shortening the lever compared with the full planche.
steps: Start in a tuck planche with straight arms on the floor or parallettes.
Extend your legs out into a wide straddle as you lean further forward.
Keep your hips and legs level with your shoulders in a straight line.
Hold the position, breathing steadily.

summary: A horizontal straight-body hold on locked arms with the legs together, the elite goal of planche training.
steps: Start in a planche lean or straddle planche on straight arms.
Lean forward and lift your legs until your body is parallel to the floor.
Keep your legs together, glutes tight and body straight from shoulders to toes.
Hold the position, breathing steadily.

summary: A push-up performed while holding a planche, keeping the feet off the floor through the whole rep.
steps: Lean into a planche on the floor or parallettes with your feet off the floor.
Bend your elbows to lower your chest while keeping the body level.
Lean further forward as you lower to stay balanced.
Press back up to straight arms without touching down.

summary: A ring exercise that lets the arms open wide and squeezes them back together, like a bodyweight chest fly.
steps: Hold the rings set at about hip height and lean into an incline plank with straight arms.
Keep a slight bend in the elbows and let your arms open out to the sides.
Lower only as far as you can control.
Squeeze your arms back together to return to the start.
mistakes: Bending the elbows into a push-up

summary: A straight-arm hang from a bar that builds grip strength and shoulder stability for pulling.
steps: Grip a bar with an overhand grip about shoulder-width apart.
Lift your feet so you hang with fully straight arms.
Keep your body still with the shoulders slightly engaged.
Hold the position, breathing steadily.

summary: A small pull from a dead hang made by depressing the shoulder blades, strengthening the shoulders for pull-ups.
steps: Hang from a bar with an overhand grip and straight arms.
Pull your shoulders down away from your ears to lift your body a few inches.
Pause briefly at the top with the arms straight.
Lower slowly back to a full hang.

summary: A horizontal pull under a low bar with a straight body, building the upper back, lats and biceps.
steps: Set a bar at about waist height and hang underneath it with your arms straight.
Grip slightly wider than shoulders and keep your body straight, heels on the floor.
Pull your chest to the bar, drawing your shoulder blades together.
Pause briefly, then lower slowly to straight arms.
mistakes: Reaching the chin instead of the chest

summary: An inverted row with the hands set wide and elbows flared, emphasizing the rear shoulders and upper back.
steps: Hang under a low bar with a grip wider than shoulder-width and arms straight.
Keep your body straight from shoulders to heels.
Pull your chest to the bar with your elbows flaring out to the sides.
Lower slowly to straight arms.

summary: A row on gymnastic rings with the feet on the floor, building back and biceps strength with added stability work.
steps: Hold the rings and walk your feet forward to lean back with straight arms.
Keep your body straight from head to heels.
Pull your chest up between the rings, drawing the shoulder blades together.
Lower slowly to straight arms.

summary: An inverted row pulled with one arm while the body stays square, building unilateral back and core strength.
steps: Hang under a low bar or ring with one hand and your body straight.
Set your feet wider for balance and place the free hand on your chest or hip.
Pull your chest toward the hand without rotating your torso.
Lower slowly to a straight arm, then switch sides.

summary: A vertical pull with palms facing away that lifts the chin over the bar, building lat, biceps and grip strength.
steps: Hang from a bar with palms facing away, hands about shoulder-width apart.
Draw your shoulders down and brace your core.
Pull your elbows down and back until your chin clears the bar.
Lower slowly to a full hang with straight arms.

summary: A pull-up with palms facing you and hands about shoulder-width, adding biceps emphasis to the lat work.
steps: Hang from a bar with palms facing you, hands shoulder-width apart or slightly closer.
Brace your core and set your shoulders down.
Pull with elbows close to your body until your chin clears the bar.
Lower slowly to a full hang.
mistakes: Stopping short of a full hang

summary: A pull-up with the hands much wider than the shoulders, emphasizing the upper lats and shoulders.
steps: Hang from a bar with an overhand grip well wider than shoulder-width.
Draw your shoulders down and keep them there.
Drive your elbows down and slightly back to pull your chest toward the bar.
Pause briefly when your chin clears the bar, then lower slowly.
mistakes: Grip so wide the range becomes very short

summary: A pull-up with the hands close together, increasing range of motion and emphasis on the biceps and grip.
steps: Hang from a bar with your hands a few inches apart.
Brace your core and set your shoulders down.
Pull your chest toward your hands until your chin clears the bar.
Lower slowly to a full hang.
mistakes: Partial range at the top or bottom

summary: A pull-up on parallel handles with palms facing each other, training the lats and biceps in a joint-friendly grip.
steps: Hang from parallel handles with your palms facing each other.
Brace your core and set your shoulders down.
Pull with elbows close to your sides until your chin clears the handles.
Lower slowly to a full hang.
mistakes: Stopping short of a full hang

summary: A pull-up with the hands close and staggered along the bar, moving the head to alternate sides on each rep.
steps: Stand under the bar side-on and grip it with hands close together, one in front of the other.
Hang with straight arms and brace your core.
Pull up so your head passes one side of the bar.
Lower slowly and pass the head to the other side on the next rep.
mistakes: Rotating the torso to get over the bar

summary: A pull-up performed with the legs held straight out in an L, training the back and the core together.
steps: Hang from a bar with an overhand grip about shoulder-width apart.
Lift your straight legs to hip height so your body forms an L.
Pull until your chin clears the bar while holding the legs level.
Lower slowly to a full hang without dropping the legs.

summary: A wide-grip pull-up that pulls the body toward one hand while the other arm stays straight, building one-arm strength.
steps: Hang from a bar with an overhand grip much wider than shoulder-width.
Pull your body toward one hand, bending that arm.
Keep the other arm straight along the bar.
Lower slowly to a full hang and repeat toward the other side.

summary: A wide pull-up that travels side to side at the top of the bar, building unilateral lat, biceps and grip strength.
steps: Hang from a bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Pull up until your chin is above the bar.
Shift toward one hand by straightening the other arm while staying at bar height.
Move smoothly across to the other hand, then lower to a full hang.

summary: A full pull-up using a single arm, demanding extraordinary lat, biceps and grip strength.
steps: Hang from a bar with one hand, palm facing you or neutral, the other arm free.
Brace your core and engage the working shoulder.
Pull until your chin clears the bar while limiting rotation.
Lower slowly to a full hang, then switch sides.
mistakes: Starting from a passive, loose shoulder

summary: A pull-up gripping towels draped over the bar, greatly increasing the demand on grip and forearms.
steps: Drape two towels over a pull-up bar and grip one firmly in each hand.
Hang with straight arms and brace your core.
Pull until your hands are near your chin.
Lower slowly to straight arms.
mistakes: Losing grip and slipping on the way down

summary: A pull-up driven with maximum speed so the chest reaches the bar or higher, building pulling power.
steps: Hang from a bar with an overhand grip about shoulder-width apart.
Brace your core and set your shoulders down.
Pull as fast and hard as you can, aiming to bring your chest to the bar or above.
Lower under control to a full hang before the next rep.

summary: A fast pull-up that turns over the bar into a dip and locks out on top, building explosive pull-to-push strength.
steps: Hang from a bar with an overhand grip about shoulder-width apart.
Pull explosively, driving the bar toward your lower chest.
As the bar reaches your chest, lean forward and turn your wrists over the bar.
Press down until your arms are straight with the bar at your waist.
Lower back through the transition to a hang with control.
mistakes: Pulling straight up instead of around the bar
One arm going over before the other
Using a large kip before you can do it strictly

summary: A muscle-up on gymnastic rings using a false grip, demanding control through the transition into a ring dip.
steps: Hang from the rings with a false grip, wrists over the rings.
Pull the rings down toward your chest, keeping them close.
Lean forward and roll your shoulders over the rings into the bottom of a dip.
Press up until your arms are straight above the rings.
Lower back through the transition to a hang with control.
mistakes: Rings drifting away from the body

summary: A hanging hold with the knees tucked and the back horizontal facing up, building lat and shoulder strength.
steps: Hang from a bar with straight arms and an overhand grip.
Pull your knees into your chest.
Press the bar down with straight arms to raise your back level with the floor.
Hold the position, breathing steadily.

summary: A hanging hold with the whole body straight and horizontal facing up, an elite test of lat and core strength.
steps: Hang from a bar with straight arms and an overhand grip.
Press the bar down with straight arms as you raise your body.
Extend your legs until your body is straight and parallel to the floor.
Hold the position, breathing steadily.
cues: Press the bar toward the hips

summary: A rowing movement performed from a front lever, pulling the bar toward the waist while staying horizontal.
steps: Hang from a bar and raise into a front lever or tuck front lever.
Bend your elbows to pull the bar toward your waist.
Keep your body horizontal throughout the pull.
Extend your arms slowly back to the lever.

summary: A rotation from a hang backward through an inverted hang to a German hang and back, building shoulder mobility.
steps: Hang from a bar or rings with straight arms.
Tuck your knees and lift them up between your arms as you rotate backward.
Continue through an inverted hang and lower your feet behind you to a comfortable range.
Reverse the motion slowly back to the hang.
mistakes: Dropping into the bottom without control
Bending the arms during the rotation

summary: A face-down horizontal hold with knees tucked, hanging below the bar to build shoulder and biceps strength.
steps: Hang from a bar or rings and rotate backward into an inverted hang.
Tuck your knees to your chest.
Lower your back slowly until it is horizontal and facing down.
Hold the position, breathing steadily.

summary: A face-down straight-body hold hanging below the bar, placing heavy demand on the shoulders and biceps.
steps: Hang from a bar or rings and rotate backward into an inverted hang.
Lower your body slowly with straight arms.
Stop when your body is straight and parallel to the floor, legs together.
Hold the position, breathing steadily.

summary: A pull-up variation that rocks the body toward and away from the bar at the top, isolating the biceps.
steps: Pull up to the top position with your chin above the bar.
Push your body away from the bar by partially straightening your arms.
Pull your body back in toward the bar without lowering.
Lower slowly to a full hang when finished.

summary: A ring curl that leans forward with the arms behind, then curls back up, a demanding biceps exercise.
steps: Hold the rings at about hip height and stand facing away from the anchor.
Lean forward with straight arms extended behind you.
Curl your elbows to pull your body back upright.
Lower forward slowly to straight arms.
mistakes: Leaning further than you can control

summary: A ring curl leaning back with a straight body, curling yourself up by bending only at the elbows.
steps: Hold the rings with palms up and walk your feet forward to lean back.
Keep your body straight from head to heels with arms extended.
Bend only your elbows to curl your hands toward your forehead.
Lower slowly to straight arms.
mistakes: Turning it into a row by pulling the elbows back

summary: A transition from the top of a pull-up out to a front lever and back, building lat and core strength.
steps: Pull up to the top position with your chin over the bar.
Push the bar away with straight arms while raising your hips and legs.
Rotate out to a front lever or tuck front lever position.
Pull yourself back up to the top of the pull-up.
mistakes: Dropping the hips in the lever
Bending at the hips through the transition

summary: A ring pull toward the face with elbows high and outward rotation, training the rear shoulders and upper back.
steps: Hold the rings with palms facing down and lean back with straight arms.
Keep your body straight from head to heels.
Pull the rings toward your face with your elbows high and wide.
Rotate your hands back at the top, then lower slowly.

summary: A standing two-leg squat to full comfortable depth, building quadriceps and glute strength.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out.
Bend your knees and hips, sitting back and down between your heels.
Lower until your thighs are at least parallel, keeping your chest up.
Push through your whole foot to return to standing.
mistakes: Rounding the back at the bottom

summary: A full single-leg squat with the free leg straight in front, building leg strength, balance and mobility.
steps: Stand on one leg with the other leg straight and slightly forward.
Reach your arms forward and bend the standing knee slowly.
Lower to full depth, keeping the free leg straight and off the floor.
Drive through the standing foot to rise, then switch sides.

summary: A single-leg squat with the free leg bent behind you, heel toward the glutes, building quadriceps strength.
steps: Stand on one leg and bend the other knee so the foot is behind you.
Hold the rear foot or keep it lifted, arms forward for balance.
Lower until the back knee lightly touches the floor.
Drive through the standing foot to rise, then switch sides.

summary: An advanced single-leg squat with the free leg crossing behind the standing leg, demanding strength and mobility.
steps: Stand on one leg with your arms reaching forward for balance.
Bend the standing knee and sweep the free leg behind and across it.
Lower toward full depth, keeping your hips and shoulders facing forward.
Drive through the standing foot to rise, then switch sides.

summary: A single-leg squat with the free leg floating behind you, building quadriceps and glute strength without support.
steps: Stand on one leg with the other knee bent and the foot lifted behind you.
Reach your arms forward and lean slightly from the hips.
Bend the standing knee to lower until the back knee nearly touches the floor.
Drive through the standing foot to rise, then switch sides.
mistakes: Back knee crashing into the floor

summary: A squat that leans back with the hips pushed forward so movement happens at the knees, isolating the quadriceps.
steps: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a support lightly if needed.
Rise onto the balls of your feet and push your hips forward.
Bend your knees forward and lean back, keeping a straight line from knees to shoulders.
Lower as far as you can control, then straighten your knees to return.
mistakes: Sitting the hips back into a normal squat
Dropping lower than you can control

summary: A deep lateral squat where one leg bends fully while the other extends to the side, training quads and adductors.
steps: Stand with your feet in a wide stance, toes turned out slightly.
Shift to one side and sit deep into that hip, keeping the heel down.
Keep the other leg straight with its toes pointing up.
Push back to the middle and repeat to the other side.
cues: Heel down on the working side

summary: A wide-stance squat that shifts the weight onto one leg while the other stays straight, building one-leg strength.
steps: Stand in a wide stance with your toes pointing forward or slightly out.
Shift your weight to one side and bend that knee as you lower.
Keep the other leg straight with its foot flat on the floor.
Push back up to the middle and repeat to the other side.

summary: A split squat with the rear foot raised on a bench, building quadriceps, glute and hamstring strength in each leg.
steps: Stand tall a long stride in front of a bench or chair.
Place the top of your rear foot on the bench behind you.
Bend the front knee until the back knee nearly touches the floor.
Push through the front foot to return to the top, then switch sides.
mistakes: Pushing off with the back leg

summary: A flowing squat with an arm swing that rises onto the toes at the bottom, training the quadriceps, calves and glutes.
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and arms reaching forward.
Swing your arms back as you squat down, letting your heels rise.
Lower to the bottom on the balls of your feet.
Swing your arms forward as you stand up, lowering your heels at the top.
